## TL;DR

I completed the Releases cut-flow QA at 1280 × 900 and 375 × 812. The notes chooser, blocked, running, failed, and successful states remained usable. The mobile drawer scrolls long content while keeping Publish/Cancel visible. No product bug surfaced, so the only code change from the QA pass is in its browser harness: review round 1 correctly pointed out that uncaught browser errors were recorded but did not fail the run. The harness now throws when the collected error list is non-empty. The full browser matrix passed again with zero release POSTs. The scoped RepoOS check is the final remaining step for this round.

## Work and rationale

I began by reading the Releases view, its existing cut-flow tests, release preview fixtures, the UI preview conventions, and the previous release/restart QA report. Existing tests already exercise Cut Next, AI notes choices, cached drafts, and form persistence. This QA task called for rendered behavior at desktop and phone widths, so I wrote a Playwright pass against the actual app rather than duplicating those component tests.

The browser script intercepts `/api/release*` and supplies synthetic release status, run, distribution, email, notes, and auto-publish data. It covers a ready state and opens the notes chooser without confirming generation, then uses separate page contexts for a dirty-tree blocker, a running check, a failed check with test output, and a succeeded run. The browser is explicitly headless. The release POST endpoint is intercepted and counted; a nonzero count fails the script. The run did not contact a real publish path, push, tag, invoke a live agent, or call the Debugger.

For each of the five states, the script checks 1280 × 900 and 375 × 812. Assertions cover horizontal overflow, chooser options and action visibility, disabled cut entry under blockers, current progress phase, failed summary, success outcome, action footer viewport bounds, and browser page errors. It records page errors to make the final output useful, and now also throws with state, viewport, and error details if any exist. That last assertion addresses review round 1.

The first pass used an isolated detached scratch worktree for `just serve-noauth 7286`; the follow-up used a fresh scratch snapshot again. Playwright ran against loopback while intercepting the release APIs. The 375px chooser, failure, and success captures were visually inspected. Generated captures live under ignored `.repoos/qa-releases-cut-flow/` and are not part of the branch.

The requested retained report is `docs/qa/2026-11-releases-cut-flow.md`. It records the responsive state matrix, safety boundary, QA setup, and both the original pass and the round 1 assertion correction. The reproduction script is `docs/qa/measure-releases-cut-flow.mjs`.

## Approaches tried

The initial browser navigation waited for `networkidle`. That never settled because the app maintains an event stream. I switched to `domcontentloaded` followed by waits for route-specific UI elements. This gives deterministic readiness and a useful failure point when the drawer does not mount.

My first locator used Playwright's default `data-testid` attribute, while this codebase uses `data-test-id`. I changed those locators to explicit CSS selectors. These were harness issues and did not require application changes.

I initially reviewed the failed view at a 900px phone height. Since the error summary and test details fill much of the screen, I added bounding-box and scroll-height measurements, then used the more representative 812px height. Measurements showed the drawer body scrolls independently and its action footer stays within the viewport. This behavior held for the long failed state.

The automated reviewer caught a real gap in my QA assertion: collecting `pageErrors` and printing them did not make the script fail. I fixed this by checking the list after each scenario and throwing a state-specific error when non-empty. I then reran all ten combinations against the scratch server. Each produced an empty `pageErrors` array and the release POST counter stayed at zero.

## Challenges and blockers

The long-lived event stream made `networkidle` unsuitable. A route-specific ready condition resolved this without changing the app. The fixture for the blocker state disables the top-level cut entry but still lets the deep link open the panel; this lets the pass inspect the explanation and panel gating without trying to circumvent any real server validation.

The review report itself was not present in the checked-out `.repoos/reviews/1206` path. The queued review message gave the precise defect, so I used that to fix the current branch after confirming through `repoos list` that #1206 had returned to `active` and the worktree was clean. I did not edit while the task was in review.

No human-only requirement blocked this pass. No real device, account, or live release credential was used. Screenshots are transient local artifacts; no binary image is tracked.

## Key learnings

For RepoOS UI browser checks, `networkidle` is unreliable because the app's event stream remains open. Waiting for a route-specific control is more stable and better scoped to the experience under test.

The Release drawer already provides the needed phone layout: the body takes the overflow and the footer remains reachable. Its failure details can be long without pushing the primary actions offscreen.

QA telemetry must have a clear failure condition. A diagnostic list only helps if the harness fails on unexpected entries. The updated script keeps the messages for diagnosis and enforces the expectation for every state and viewport.

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the final tree. The changed-path run classified this as docs/bookkeeping-only, so unrelated build, lint, test, and UI smoke steps were skipped; formatting, branch-artifact, task-asset, and task-parser checks passed. I did not stage or commit files; RepoOS owns task-branch finalization.
